# seok · blog

> Notes by Seokwon Choi, developer. Mostly technical, plus whatever else comes up along the way. Every post exists in Korean and English, each as plain markdown.

## Posts

- [A tour of this blog: diagrams, math, code](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/tour/en.md): The first post. Everything this blog can put inside a post, one thing at a time: a figure that follows your place, diagrams drawn at build time, math, code, and two languages. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/tour/ko.md
- [Why Hangul takes two columns in a terminal](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/hangul-width/en.md): Why one Hangul syllable is as wide as two Latin letters, why arrows and box-drawing characters change width from one setup to the next, and why string length is not a column count. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/hangul-width/ko.md
- [Powersort in CPython 3.11: the merge order list.sort changed](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/cpython-powersort/en.md): In Python 3.11 the rule that decides which runs list.sort merges switched from timsort's stack invariants to powersort's boundary powers. This post walks through what changed in code and measures comparison counts and time on 3.10 and 3.11. Random input does not move at all; only runs of uneven length do. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/cpython-powersort/ko.md
- [Redis HyperLogLog: counting a million users in 14 KB](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-hyperloglog/en.md): Counting unique visitors with a SET takes 48 MB for a million; HyperLogLog takes 14 KB. How it counts, and how far off it is, measured. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-hyperloglog/ko.md
- [Go 1.22 loop variables: the fixed bug and one line of go.mod](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/go122-loopvar/en.md): Since Go 1.22, for-loop variables are created fresh on every iteration. But the go line in go.mod, not the toolchain, decides which semantics apply, and go run main.go never reads that line. I checked both toolchains, and measured a loop that leaks addresses going from 2 to 102 allocations. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/go122-loopvar/ko.md
- [Redis listpack: between field 512 and field 513](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-listpack/en.md): In Redis 7, small hashes, sets and zsets live in a single listpack. One step past the threshold triples memory, a converted encoding never comes back, and raising the threshold turns lookups into a linear scan. Measured on Redis 7.2. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-listpack/ko.md
- [Is a cuckoo filter really better than a Bloom filter?](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/cuckoo-vs-bloom/en.md): The cuckoo filter paper is subtitled Practically Better Than Bloom. Implementing both and measuring load factor by bucket size, false-positive rate at equal space, and deletion shows it is not always true. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/cuckoo-vs-bloom/ko.md
- [Jump Consistent Hash: consistent hashing in five lines and no memory](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/jump-consistent-hash/en.md): Growing from 10 to 11 buckets, mod-N moves 91% of keys and Jump Consistent Hash moves 9.1%. How it does that with no ring and no table, measured next to a hash ring. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/jump-consistent-hash/ko.md
- [What actually runs when you call sort(): quicksort in C++, Rust and Go](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/sorting-in-the-wild/en.md): Textbook quicksort goes quadratic on an already sorted array, so none of the C++, Rust or Go standard libraries ship it. This post follows libstdc++'s introsort, the pdqsort in Rust and Go 1.19, and the three stable sorts, with animations showing which input each one defends against and how. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/sorting-in-the-wild/ko.md
- [Skip lists: from coin flips to Redis rankings](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/skip-list/en.md): A few tall nodes shorten a search. Redis adds rank accounting; LevelDB turns the structure into a memory index that can be read during writes. Change the paths and spans, then follow where the papers and production implementations diverge. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/skip-list/ko.md
- [A Field Guide to Redis Caching: Expiry, Eviction, and the Herd at the Door](https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-cache-field-guide/en.md): A cache is easy to add and hard to run. I read how expiry and eviction actually work in the Redis 6.2 source, then measured a cache stampede and approximate LRU. Interview glossary, quiz, and flash cards at the end. Korean: https://alfex4936.github.io/blog/redis-cache-field-guide/ko.md
